newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: JULL SAYS FRAUD FRENZY OVER THE TOP
The Administrative Services Minister, David Jull, says what he calls a frenzy going on about alleged fraud by Members of Parliament, is probably a bit over the top.
Mr Jull, says he'll receive a report tomorrow on an investigation into Senator Mal Colston's use of Commonwealth Cars.
Mr Jull says parliamentarians might sometimes "trip over the edge" a little bit, but there are checks and balances in the system to make sure there's no massive fraud.
The Minister says it'll be at least May before new accounting procedures are implemented to check politicians' expenses, and he's promised any rorting will be stopped.
BORBIDGE SEES SUPPORT FOR QLD IN ABORIGINES' STANCE
Queensland's Premier says a delegation of Gulf country Aborigines have confirmed the view of his Government that the Native Title Act needs to be amended.
The representatives of the Waanyi and Mingginda people have told the Prime Minister he must make sure the Century Zinc mine goes ahead.
They've also called for the act to be amended.
Rob Borbidge says their stance backs the Queensland Government's approach to native title in the wake of the High Court's Wik decision.
PARER WARNS ON NATIVE TITLE UNCERTAINTY
The Federal Resources minister says it will take five years for the loss of investment in Australia's mining and pastoral industries to be felt as a result of Native Title uncertainty.
Warwick Parer says the Native Title Act must be changed, and legislation introduced to over-ride the High Court's Wik decision.
Senator Parer says the collapse of negotiations over Queensland's Century Zinc mine is a disgrace, and highlights the failures of the current laws.
He says the majority of Aboriginal people in the area recognised the benefits of the Century project, and supported it.
Mr Parer says legislation needs to ensure a few dissident protestors can't bring down entire projects.
TASSIE'S ANTI-GAY LAWS TO FACE HIGH COURT CHALLENGE
The path has been cleared for a High Court challenge to Tasmania's anti-homosexual laws.
The High Court today dismissed an application from the Tasmanian Government to set aside the challenge by activist, Rodney Croome.
Mr Croome can now proceed to the country's highest court with his claim that the anti-gay laws are invalid under the constitution.
MAN JAILED FOR SETTING CAT TRAP
A Victorian man with a previous conviction for cruelty to animals will spend the next four months in jail after setting a steel-jawed trap to catch his neighbour's cat.
Andrew Buckland was convicted in Ringwood Magistrate's Court.
The cat's owner, Charles Almond, says he called the R-S-P-C-A after his children discovered the cat, Rex, on Mr Buckland's property.
He says he released Rex and, under instructions from the R-S-P-C-A, photographed him before taking him to the vet.
Rex has made a full recovery.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
